standard.title: Reflect to inform choreographic choices
standard.description: reflect on own and others' use of the elements of dance, choreographic devices, structure, genre- or style-specific techniques and/or technical and expressive skills to inform their choreographic or performance choices
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can reflect on own and others' dance works and/or practices to inform choreographic choices and use of technical and expressive skills (Y7-8, AC9ADA8D02). They can use journals and peer feedback as reflective tools.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on own and others' use of elements, choreographic devices, structure, genre- or style-specific techniques and/or technical and expressive skills to inform their choreographic or performance choices.

nodes.label: Analytical reflection using Viewpoints
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use Viewpoints-based evaluation to analyse element and device use in their own and others' work — connecting analysis to specific choreographic or performance choices.
nodes.minimum_width: Using at least two Viewpoints questions to reflect analytically on a specific aspect of own or another's work — connecting analysis to at least one decision.
nodes.typical_width: Using Viewpoints to reflect on and evaluate forms and elements: 'How can I use space and dynamics to convey my ideas?'; evaluating choreographic and performance choices ('How successful were the dancers in conveying the stated intent?', 'What was the impact of choosing gesture to communicate emotion?'); documenting in reflective records.
wider: Maintain a systematic reflective journal across an extended choreographic project — analysing key decision points and their outcomes
Analyse a professional dance work for element and device use — applying the same analytical frame to their own choreographic process

response_modes.reason: Analytical reflection — not just impressionistic response — requires a consistent evaluative framework. Viewpoints questions provide this frame; students need practice using them analytically before using them generatively.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who develop analytical reflection as a systematic practice gain a self-directed learning tool that continues to support development beyond formal study — this is a metacognitive capability, not just a dance skill.
success_criteria: Student uses at least two Viewpoints questions to analyse specific element or device use in a dance work
Student connects the analysis to a specific choreographic or performance decision

nodes.label: Reflecting on personal identity and influence
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on how personal identity, emotions, political positions and critical theories influence and shape their approach to dance.
nodes.minimum_width: Identifying at least one personal influence (cultural identity, emotion, interest) that shapes their choreographic choices — connecting it to a specific decision.
nodes.typical_width: Improvising using elements of dance and analysing movement choices to reflect individuality and clarify choreographic intent; considering how emotion, political statements, critical theories or lived experiences influence approach to dance; documenting creative process including analysis and evaluation.
wider: Explore how their cultural background or identity influences their choreographic choices — comparing this with how other choreographers' identities shape their work
Investigate a choreographer whose political or social identity is central to their practice — analysing how personal position is translated into choreographic choices
nodes.hinge_reason: Personal voice and reflective identity awareness are what distinguish creative work at senior level from technical reproduction. Students who cannot yet connect personal influence to choreographic choice produce work that is stylistically competent but personally unmotivated.

response_modes.reason: Personal reflection integrates analytical skill (N1) with self-knowledge and creative ownership. Frame as: 'Your choreographic choices reveal something about you — what do you want them to reveal?'

success_criteria: Student identifies at least one personal influence that shapes their choreographic approach — connecting it to a specific decision
Student can explain how a specific element of their identity or perspective is expressed through their choreographic or movement choices
